Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Kraków shooting — President Nawrocki and PM Tusk join thousands at silent march; prosecutors treat attack as terrorist offence
Europe.location: Main Market Square, Kraków, and Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, Poland
Europe.summary: AP, BBC, Sky News, AFP and Al Jazeera report that Polish police say the 24-year-old gunman, who killed six people and wounded 15 in Kraków's Main Market Square on Saturday, has died in hospital. Anadolu says the victims were four women and two men and that prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation. Al Hadath reports police found the bodies of the attacker's parents and sister at his home. AFP says authorities described him as "fascinated by far-right ideologies"; the motive assessment remains preliminary. AFP reports prosecutors said his reasons for killing nine people, including three family members, remain unclear. Reuters reports Poland held a march for the victims on Monday. Al Jazeera reports prosecutors are treating the attack as a terrorist offence while the motive remains unknown, and names the gunman as 24-year-old Michal Oksinski. Al Jazeera reports President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk joined thousands at the march of silence.
Europe.status: Gunman dead; motive unknown; toll reporting differs (six killed in the square, nine including three family members); Al Jazeera reports president and PM joined the silent march; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found
